known_limitations: Coverage: 2.3%-11.0% of admitted-schedule games per season have no play-by-play in the pinned assets (worst in 2015); those fixtures are NO_DATA for any 1H purpose.

Integrity gate (mandatory): Method-A derived finals disagree with the admitted schedule finals on 1.1%-1.9% of joined games per season; adjudication (9/9 sampled) sides with the schedule - the class is PBP-feed defects. A fixture's halftime may be consumed only when its derived final equals the schedule final.

Method B (summing score_value over scoring_play-flagged rows) is NOT a valid derivation in any era and is refused: the scoring_play flag is unreliable (unflagged made baskets, score updates on non-play rows) and isolated early-era feeds contain duplicated segments that inflate sums.

Halftime cross-check source is ESPN's own published linescores - a different artifact and endpoint, but the same provider as the PBP; no independent-provenance halftime source exists in the program (the CBR logs carry finals only).
Rolling release: all 27 in-window assets carried updated_at 2026-10-18 at pull time; pins attest the bytes as pulled, nothing more.
pin_rule: tag + release ID + asset ID + asset size + asset updated_at + SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes, all recorded in this manifest at pull time, together with the pull timestamp (retrieved_at_utc). The release is ROLLING (assets replaced in place under a stable tag), so the pin attests the bytes as pulled at retrieved_at_utc - the strongest attestation this source supports; it does NOT attest that upstream bytes are stable or immutable. Any later byte drift against this manifest is SOURCE_CHANGED_AFTER_SNAPSHOT (refusal), never silent acceptance.

sample_checks.sample_design: 36 games chosen deterministically from the admitted schedules before any PBP content was read: per season the earliest game, the latest game (the championship game in tournament seasons), and the games at the one-third and two-thirds positions of the date-sorted schedule

derivation.column_order_note: Column ORDER differs between seasons (e.g. 2015 vs 2017+); the column SET differs only as listed in era_diffs. Consumers must read by field name, never by position.
derivation.method_a_running_score: A team's first-half points are its running score (away_score/home_score) at the end of period 1 - the maximum of its running score over period_number == 1 rows. Finals likewise over all rows. This is the admitted derivation.
derivation.method_b_scoring_sum_status: REFUSED - summing score_value over rows with scoring_play == 'true' grouped by team_id is not a valid derivation in any era: the flag is unreliable in the feed (made baskets with scoring_play false; score increments landing on End Period / foul rows in later seasons) and isolated early-era game feeds contain duplicated segments that inflate the sum. Recorded as a negative schema finding.
derivation.period_values_observed: period_number 1-2 are the halves; 3+ are overtime periods (observed maximum 6 in 2015-2018, 2020, 2022, 2023; 5 in 2019 and 2021)
